contentBlocks.text: This week you learned to study religion respectfully, including your own tradition. Let's review it all!

Quick review: comparative religion is the respectful, humble study of traditions side by side (Day 1). Many traditions address similar universal questions in their own way (Day 2). This connects to Sikhi's own historical commitment to pluralism, from Langar to the Sikh Empire (Day 3). You applied this framework to reflect on Sikhi itself (Day 4). Write a short paragraph explaining how studying comparative religion with humility connects back to Sikhi's own value of equality.
Great work this week — you learned to study religion, including your own, with real humility and respect! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review comparative religion, universal questions, the civic-life connection, and personal reflection
Explain how comparative religion's humility connects to Sikhi's value of equality
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child write their connecting paragraph about humility and equality.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of comparative religion!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one specific historical example (Langar) rather than requiring a fully abstract connection
Ready for more: ask the child how they might explain the value of comparative religion to a friend who's never thought about it before
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four comparative-religion ideas needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended synthesis activity — check that the paragraph connects comparative religion's core value of humility (not claiming to fully understand or judge another tradition from outside) to Sikhi's own value of equality (treating everyone, regardless of background, with the same dignity and respect).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's comparative-religion thread and the C3 Framework's Civics dimension before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
